"A camera with video output feed. Has infrared mode as well as a variable field of view."

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Camera Medium | |
| [Camera medium](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/stormworks_gamepedia_en/images/8/86/Camera_medium.png/revision/latest?cb=20220212042521) | |
| Mass | 10 |
| Dimensions | 1×2×1 |
| Cost | $3,000 |
| Logic inputs | Bool (Infrared mode), Numeric (Field of view) |
| Logic outputs | Video (Camera feed) |
| Connections | Electric |
| Since version | [V0.7.1](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/V0.7.1 "V0.7.1") |

## Notes

A [camera](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Building/Components/Video/Cameras "Wiki/Building/Components/Video/Cameras") with telescopic and wide-field zoom capabilities, as well as [infrared mode](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Infrared_mode "Infrared mode"). It has a wide range of uses, including all of those for the [small camera](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Camera_small "Camera small") as well as more advanced applications like being placed on a weapon turret to zoom in and track distant [radar](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Radar "Radar") contacts, allowing the player to positively identify them.

### FOV / Zoom

The camera's numeric FOV input will take values from 0-1 (anything higher or lower has no additional effect) and has a zoom range of 0.29x up to 28x zoom.

0 is the low-zoom wide field of view, with the camera seeing a 127-degree vertical FOV (0.29x zoom). 1 is the high-zoom narrow field of view, with the camera seeing an approximately 1.43 degree FOV (0.025 radian FOV - 28x zoom). The camera's FOV setting is structured so that the number of degrees in its FOV increases evenly as the input value increases, so adding 0.5 to a low input value will add (127-1.43)\*0.5 degrees to the FOV.

The following function can be used in a function block or Lua block in a [microcontroller](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Microcontroller "Microcontroller") to convert from desired zoom (x) to the required input value for the camera:

1-(2\*(180/pi)\*(atan (tan ((pi/180)\*(70/2.0))/x)))/(127-1.43)

The formula to go back from a camera zoom to FOV is

0.700208/tan(0.0053+1.16562\*x)

The formula to go from a camera input to FOV is

(1-x)\*2.1893+0.025

The same logic can be used for adjusting camera zoom when tracking targets at a distance. Once you've picked a desirable zoom setting for 100m, you can simply divide the target's distance by 100, multiply by the desired zoom for 100m, and then input that desired zoom (x) into the function above.

content.markdown:
Vehicles can be damaged in Stormworks in many different ways. In the base game, there is the risk of colliding vehicles with other vehicles or terrain. Additionally, an engine which runs too fast and is inadequately cooled can overheat and catch on fire. Fire can spread to nearby walls and components causing gradually spreading damage. There are also some [missions](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Missions "Wiki/Missions") which create substantial risk of vehicle damage, e.g. towing an old sea mine to a port. With the [Search and Destroy DLC](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Search_and_Destroy_DLC "Search and Destroy DLC"), enemy vehicles may also fire guns, rockets, and missiles at player-made vehicles. With the many different ways vehicles can be damaged, it is good practice to prepare vehicles to be able to survive the damage and recover.

## Damage propagation

Damage can spread by fire, by ammunition cookoff, or by warhead detonation.

Damaged batteries and engines can catch on fire. The fire can spread across anything, even normal blocks, unless/until is extinguished. A single uncontrolled fire can eventually destroy an entire ship or aircraft.

Damaged ammo drums which contain ammo can cook off. Several rounds of whatever ammo type they contain will be shot out in random directions around the drum. Large quantities of ammo packed together can easily cause a rapid chain reaction.

Torpedo, missile, and bomb warheads can explode if they are damaged. If they are positioned near each other and one is damaged, it can lead to almost instantaneous detonation of the entire group. EMP warheads will also trigger their EMP effect if damaged.

Rocket launchers, battle cannon belts, artillery cannon belts, and Bertha cannon belts are all safe to damage without risk of chain reaction.

## Bulkheads

Dividing a large ship or submarine into several sections separated by walls along its length and width can help to contain flooding.

### Collision risk

The front of a ship is the area most likely to be damaged in a collision, so the front bulkhead area is generally the most important. To prevent fires it should not contain batteries, ammo, or fuel-driven engines. Additionally, it needs to be sized appropriately. If it's too small, the bulkhead may be damaged along with the hull, leading to further flooding behind it. Thus, it needs to be designed large enough to contain the damage but not overly large so that it remains easy to bilge out if it floods.

## Fire detection

Temperature sensors can detect the added heat of a fire. Once the sensor is broken, it will suddenly report a temperature of exactly 0. A high temperature or 0 temperature can both be taken as signs that an area is likely to have an active fire.

## Fire suppression

At the very least, nearly every vehicle should carry a fire extinguisher. A small upgrade from this for ships likely to have large fires to put out is to include a water pipe running down the length of the vessel supplied by a large pump. With numerous hose attachment points on this pipe, a player can attach a hose to one of the points and use it as a fire extinguisher with unlimited supply.

Where possible, components most likely to catch on fire if damaged, like diesel engines and batteries, should have automatic fire suppression systems. This can be accomplished with fluid cannon nozzles set to a wide spray, or with fluid cannons configured with micro-controllers to automatically spray an area. Temperature sensors can automatically detect that the area is hot (or has been damaged, which would mean probably on fire) and trigger the fluid cannons to douse the fire.

## Repair

[![Fully damaged surface repaired at the red block. Welding torch and mounted welder produce the same result.](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/stormworks_gamepedia_en/images/8/89/Welding_torch_repair.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/180?cb=20250819001905)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/stormworks_gamepedia_en/images/8/89/Welding_torch_repair.png/revision/latest?cb=20250819001905)

Fully damaged surface repaired at the red block. Welding torch and mounted welder produce the same result.

Repair can be done with by hand with welders or underwater welders, or with a vehicle using mounted welders. Most vehicles should have at least a welder and underwater welder for basic manual repairs. Mounted welders use large amounts of electricity but can be run semi-autonomously, e.g. placed on a track and moved down the the length of a ship to weld everything damaged along the hull. They can also reach places that are too small for a player to get into, e.g. a 2x2 tunnel through a ship could fit a compact rail and several welders that weld everything in all directions around the length of the tunnel.

### Lingering effects

Even after being repaired, batteries will still be depleted. Ammo drums that cooked off will be depleted of ammo.

Note that fluid tanks and gas tanks will *not* lose their contents if damaged. Also, warheads that were part of a vehicle/subvehicle which was not too damaged to continue existing can be repaired and detonated again.

## Redundancy

For critical systems, like power, it's generally a good idea to have a redundant backup.

For example, note that a damaged battery will still have zero power after repair. If you needed the battery to start your engine and needed the engine to charge your battery, then you may be left with an inoperable vehicle that you can't get working again. Having a backup battery in a separate location and a circuit breaker to protect it against being drained will allow you to fix your damaged main battery, restart your engine, and then recharge both batteries.

### Manual backups

Hand cranks can be a very useful way to either manually crank an engine to start (if the starter has insufficient power), or to provide initial charge to a battery so basic systems like throttles, buttons, clutches, and starters can be used.

Be aware that clutches do not work without power and they are commonly used to limit power taken by generators. If there's only one battery and one generator and the generator takes power from the engine through a clutch then in the event of battery damage there will be no way to get the vehicle running again unless/until it can be jumpstarted. For this typical situation, it is good practice to have one or two handcranks connected to the generator *after* the clutch.

Note that hand cranks turn slowly, usually less than 1 rpm, but have decent torque. Three [gearboxes](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Guides/Gearbox "Wiki/Guides/Gearbox") set to 3:1 with the arrows facing towards the handcrank(s) and a small generator are an effective way to recharge a small battery enough to start an engine within a few minutes.

### Auxiliary power units (APUs)

See [auxiliary power unit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auxiliary_power_unit) at Wikipedia.

Many real-life aircraft carry an engine and generator solely dedicated to providing power for the aircraft. As the name suggests, this is a dedicated backup system. Generators connected to the main engines provide all power under normal circumstances, although the APU may be used to initially power up the aircraft before takeoff if ground power is unavailable. Further, in the event of simultaneous engine failure, the APU can be switched on in-flight to maintain power to control surfaces, fuel pumps, landing gear hydraulics, de-icing systems, and life support to buy time for the engine failure to be diagnosed and corrected, or, if all else fails, to at least facilitate an attempted [deadstick landing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deadstick_landing).

For Stormworks, much of the same logic applies. If an aircraft has just one battery at the bottom of the hull and it gets hit by a single round of ammo from a rotary autocannon, the engines will likely shut down in most designs, because:

- If a throttle is used to control engine throttle, an unpowered throttle will suddenly output 0, resulting in engine shutdown.

- If a clutch is used, an unpowered clutch will stop working resulting in total loss of power transmission from the engine to the rotor / propellers.

- If any electric [pumps](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Pumps "Pumps") are used (e.g. pumps acting as superchargers/turbochargers), these will shut down, blocking all air flow to the engine.

In addition to likely loss of engine power, all control surfaces will shut down, landing gears will be inoperable, pumps for fire suppression systems will not run, and mounted welders will be unable to repair the situation. With a backup battery, electric relay, backup generator, and appropriate microcontroller, the aircraft could automatically get power back on, extinguish the fire(s), and repair the main battery along with any other critical systems protected by mounted welders.

Note that a basic APU can be made with a small diesel engine, a gearbox set at 3:2 (arrows facing the engine), and a medium generator. The generator will produce 36 swatts while the engine will run at 8.16 rps and consume 0.06L of diesel per second. The power is a bit more than enough to run one mounted welder at a time.

## External links

Stormworks has a variety of equipment, including outfits, tools, weapons, and gadgets with a wide variety of uses. Players have 8 small equipment slots, 1 large equipment slot, and 1 outfit slot. Carrying equipment reduces move speed in proportion to its weight.

A lot of equipment is battery-operated and can be recharged by putting it back into an equipment rack which has power available; some non-battery operated equipment also can be replenished when put into a powered equipment rack, like oxygen masks.

## Small Equipment

Small equipment fits into a 1x1 equipment rack. Players can carry eight items of small equipment at a time.

- **Flashlight:** Replaced the pre-1.0 Headlamp. Battery-powered, shines a cone of light ahead of you. Recharges slowly in a powered locker.
- **Binoculars:** Allows you to zoom in further. Doesn't use power or require charging.
- **First Aid Kit:** Heals you, other players, or NPCs. Maximum (also default) stack of 4, consumable. Each use restores about half of a full health bar for a player or NPC, or a full health bar for a [Stormwoof](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Stormwoof "Stormwoof").
- **Night Vision Binoculars:** Battery-powered, allows you to zoom in with [night vision](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Infrared_mode "Infrared mode"). Does not allow regular vision.
- **Oxygen Mask:** Allows you to breathe in an environment without oxygen or excessive CO2, but much more limited capacity than SCUBA or diving gear. It offers 10 breaths, approximately enough for two minutes. Left click needed to breathe. Quickly refills when in a powered locker.
- **Compass:** Has two needles, the white points south, the red points north. Doesn't use power or require charging. Shows you what bearing you are facing in degrees shown above the compass' position in the equipment slot where it was placed.
- **Radio:** Battery-powered; can be used to chat with other players on the same channel (limited to channels 0-8) with a maximum effective range of 500 meters. Can also be used to signal vehicles with speakers (which produce an on/off output when receiving voice data from a linked radio channel), allowing for limited [radio](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Gameplay/Workbench/Components/Radio "Gameplay/Workbench/Components/Radio") control.
- **Remote Control Unit:** Battery-powered; allows you to remotely control a vehicle (as long as you set it up correctly). Limited to using radio channels 0-8, and an effective range of up to 500 meters.
- **Glowstick:** Provides hands-free illumination, works underwater. Lasts for somewhere between 25-30 minutes. Maximum (also default) stack of 12.
- **Flare:** Allows you to throw a road flare, provides very bright hands-free illumination, works underwater. Lasts for five minutes. Maximum (also default) stack of 4, consumable.
- **Flare Gun Ammo:** Maximum (also default) stack of 4. Used for reloading the Flare Gun. Can be refilled by unloading the Flare Gun, consumable.
- **Flare Gun:** Fires a flare in the direction you are facing (usually with an angle limit), contains one flare by default. Can be unloaded to refill Flare Gun Ammo (if you have it equipped).
- **Transponder:** Battery-powered, transmits a transponder signal, can be switched to MOB mode to activate automatically in water, has a battery meter
- **Strobe Light:** Battery-powered, model identical to transponder, flashes a strobe light when turned on, has a battery meter. Can be set to MOB (man overboard) mode like the transponder.
- **Strobe Light (IR):** Model identical to transponder, flashes a strobe light in [IR](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Infrared_mode "Infrared mode") when turned on, has a battery meter. Can be set to MOB mode like the regular strobe light and transponder.
- **Radiation Detector:** A small battery-operated Geiger counter.

### Weapon DLC

The [Weapon DLC](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Weapon_DLC "Weapon DLC") added:

- **Pistol:** A short-ranged semi-automatic pistol with a magazine capacity of 17 rounds.
- **C4 Explosive:** Can be placed on vehicles or terrain and remotely detonated.
- **C4 Detonator:** Remotely detonates any C4 placed by the player.
- **Hand Grenade:** Can be thrown a short distance - only accurate when standing still and throwing. Detonates after a short delay.
- **Pistol ammo:** An extra 17-round pistol magazine, Consumable.
- **SMG ammo:** An extra 40-round SMG magazine, Consumable.
- **Rifle ammo:** An extra 30-round rifle magazine, Consumable.
- **Speargun ammo:** Maximum(also default) stacked by 8 of speargun ammo, Consumable.

## Large Equipment

Large equipment fits in a 3x1 equipment rack. Players can only carry one item of large equipment at a time.

- **Fire Extinguisher:** Puts out fires. Carries a maximum of 9L of water and cannot be refilled.

Impact sensors detect when they are accelerated beyond their set limit. They were initially added for the [Weapon DLC](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Weapon_DLC "Weapon DLC") to serve as triggers for warheads. Note that they are no longer strictly required for that purpose since, as of [V1.3.14](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/V1.3.14 "V1.3.14"), warheads have been modified to have built-in impact sensing capability.

## Uses

- Autonomous vehicle damage detection: Unmanned tanker ships making trips to the arctic may run into moving icebergs. Such ships should normally have very low acceleration, but an iceberg collision could easily set off an impact sensor, allowing it to trigger a distress signal and get a player to fix it.

- Complex warhead triggers: Some missile designs are intended to have multiple sensors to trigger them (e.g. impact or proximity), and sometimes several conditions to prevent activation (e.g. proximity to friendly vehicles) especially with long-range effects like [EMP warheads](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Weapon_DLC#EMP_Warheads "Weapon DLC")). For these, a microcontroller may combine data from radar, an impact sensor, and [radio](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Building/Components/Radio "Wiki/Building/Components/Radio") to trigger a 0-threshold warhead only when it is appropriate to do so.

Visibility comparison on a dark night. Regular camera mode up top, infrared on the bottom. Target is illuminated by a regular light, and there is an infrared laser.

Infrared mode (nightvision) is used by the [camera medium](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Camera_medium "Camera medium"), [camera gimbal](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Camera_gimbal "Camera gimbal"), [camera stabilized](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Camera_stabilized "Camera stabilized"), and [night vision binoculars](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Equipment#Small_Equipment "Equipment"). It is useful for seeing in dim light.

## Effect

Infrared mode significantly increases the brightness of the image, adds a grain effect, makes the image grayscale (black and white), and somewhat reduces the field of view to a circle around the center of the image.

Contrary to what the name would suggest, infrared mode is not thermal infrared, and cannot see things merely because they are hot (such as engines, people, and weapon barrels). It still requires illumination, just much less than regular vision.

## Lights

Regular lights, searchlights, and spotlights all have a toggleable parameter to set them to infrared mode. In this mode, their light will be invisible to the naked eye, yet still retain their usual visibility for nightvision binoculars and cameras in infrared mode.

Note that RGB lights and indicator lights do not have an infrared parameter.

## Strobes

[Infrared strobe lights](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Equipment#Small_Equipment "Equipment") can be worn to allow infrared cameras to spot someone while regular vision would not.

## Lasers

Laser distance sensors and the [camera stabilized](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Camera_stabilized "Camera stabilized") both produce lasers, and both have a toggleable parameter to make their lasers use infrared mode. As with lights, regular lasers are visible both to the naked eye and to infrared cameras, yet infrared lasers are only visible to infrared cameras.

## Flares

[Flare launchers](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Flare_launcher "Flare launcher") can deploy flares that produce infrared light. Note that these flares still produce a significant amount of visible light, though perhaps only 1/4 that of regular flares. These flares can actually produce enough light to be blinding to infrared cameras, though if fired high in the air can serve as a good source of illumination for nighttime search and rescue operations.

Radar detectors output an 'on' value when the vehicle is detected by [radar](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Radar "Radar") from another vehicle. Note that this is not directional, and positioning of the detector does not matter. Multiple radar detectors at various locations on the same vehicle will all have matching outputs.

Also note that vehicles will not detect themselves with their own radar. Even a disconnected part from the vehicle (e.g. the radar on a missile launched from a vehicle) will neither detect the vehicle itself nor set off its radar detector. Of course, radar can still detect friendly, civilian, or hostile vehicles and set off their radar detectors.

Intermittent 'on' signals generally indicate that the vehicle has been detected by another vehicle with a radar in a sweep or scan mode, which may be used to orient turrets towards nearby vehicles. Persisent 'on' signals ("radar locks") generally indicate that the vehicle is being tracked by another vehicle with a radar in static mode, commonly used by launched missiles and unmanned weapon turrets locked onto a target. If a radar lock is detected, radar can be used to determine if there is an approaching missile, while [Flare Launchers](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Flare_Launcher "Flare Launcher") loaded with chaff can be used as a decoy to attempt to divert attacks from missiles and autoturrets.

The **Weapons DLC** (officially known as **Search and Destroy**) was released on October 5, 2021. The DLC allows players to use weapons such as cannons, autocannons, bombs, missiles, and torpedoes. It also allows players to make worlds where enemy vehicles spawn and capture islands and locations. [Click here to purchase the DLC on Steam.](https://store.steampowered.com/app/1542360/Stormworks_Search_and_Destroy/?curator_clanid=28842908)

This page was last updated for Stormworks V1.15.12 (19 March 2026), which armor piercing ammo is calculated based on the density times the thickness, rather than calculated by walls.

## Machine guns

[![Machine gun](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/stormworks_gamepedia_en/images/5/5a/Machine_gun.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/200?cb=20220129172950)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/stormworks_gamepedia_en/images/5/5a/Machine_gun.png/revision/latest?cb=20220129172950)

Machine guns are fed by hand-loaded belts of 100 rounds each. They produce little damage, but are lightweight and inexpensive.

- Cost: $50 (machine gun), $20 (ammo box), $1/round (kinetic), $2/round (AP or incendiary)
- Mass: 10 units (100 kg) [machine gun], 5 units (50 kg) [ammo box]
- Burst fire rate: 900 rounds per minute (4 ticks per round)
- Maximum burst fire duration: 3.33 seconds (manual reload required after this)
- Muzzle velocity: 800 m/s
- Projectile lifetime (ticks): 120
- Maximum range: Approx. 500 m
- Drag Coefficient: 0.005

Ammo effects:

- Kinetic: Only damages the block it hits directly (very low power compared to kinetic rounds from every other vehicle weapon).
- Armor piercing: Can pierce through 3 mass unit/block \* block length
- Incendiary: ~5% chance per shot per shot of starting a fire at the impact point. No penetration.

Machine guns can be edited in xml allowing for many modifications (Infinite ammo is needed in some cases). Changing width changes the spread. Changing length changes the projectile speed and damage. Removing completely width creates an invisible weapon.

## Autocannons

Autocannons are fast-firing weapon systems with higher damage than machine guns, though they can overheat and shut down until they have cooled off. They can be automatically reloaded by connectors, junctions, and feeders, making it possible to design a single autocannon which draws from a massive ammo stockpile within a vehicle. Vehicles can similarly be reloaded automatically from other vehicles via connectors. Manual reloading is still possible, like with machine guns, though not required.

Autocannons come in three varieties which will be described below. In order of decreasing ammo capacity (larger rounds) and increasing damage they are: light, rotary, and heavy.

Autocannons can fire five types of rounds: kinetic, high explosive, fragmentation, armor piercing and incendiary. The effects of these ammo types are described in each of the autocannon sections, since the effectiveness of the ammo increases with the more powerful autocannon variants (though at the cost of reduced ammo capacity).

All rounds damage a larger radius as the size goes up (detailed for each weapon), probability of incendiary rounds starting a fire goes up with the larger rounds,

The same small, medium, and large ammo boxes are used for all three autocannons:

- Autocannon ammo drum (small): Mass: 10 units (100 kg). Cost: $100 each.
- Autocannon ammo drum (medium): Mass: 20 units (200 kg). Cost: $100 each (same as small).
- Autocannon ammo drum (large): Mass: 40 units (400 kg). Cost: $100 each (same as small).

### Light autocannons

Light autocannons are single-barrel weapons with a relatively low fire rate and damage.

[![Light autocannon](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/stormworks_gamepedia_en/images/b/b6/Light_autocannon.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/200?cb=20220129172334)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/stormworks_gamepedia_en/images/b/b6/Light_autocannon.png/revision/latest?cb=20220129172334)

- Cost: $100 (light autocannon), $1/round (kinetic), $2/round (HE, frag, AP, and incendiary)
- Mass: 25 units (250 kg)
- Burst fire rate: 450 rounds/minute (8 ticks per round)
- Maximum burst fire duration: 14.6 seconds
- Cooldown time: 6.266 seconds
- Maximum sustained fire rate: 319 rounds/minute
- Ammo drum capacity: 500 rounds (large), 200 rounds (medium), 100 rounds (small)
- Muzzle velocity: 1,000 m/s
- Projectile lifetime (ticks): 150
- Maximum range: Approx. 750 m
- Drag Coefficient: 0.02

Ammo effects:

- Kinetic: Damages blocks up to half a meter (2 block lengths) away from the impact point. No penetration.
- High explosive: Damages blocks up to half a meter (2 block lengths) away from the impact point. No penetration.

Heavy cannons can store a single round of ammo in each belt component.

With the exception of EMP warheads, all warheads are high explosive. They come in small, medium, and large sizes, and can be activated by receiving damage, by impact (if armed and an impact threshold set), or detonated by logic (when armed and no impact threshold set). Warheads are used to make missiles, bombs, heavy rockets, sea mines, depth charges, torpedoes, and self-destruct devices. ### Small warheads

These damage everything within 2.5 meters (10 blocks) of the warhead's position when it detonates, a slightly greater damage radius than rockets. Well-suited for use as small missile warheads or cluster munitions.

- Cost: $25
- Mass: 15 (150 kg)

### Medium warheads

[![Warhead medium](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIABAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAEALAAAAAABAAEAQAICTAEAOw%3D%3D)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/stormworks_gamepedia_en/images/4/45/Warhead_medium.png/revision/latest?cb=20220129230324)

These damage everything within 3.25 meters (13 blocks) of the warhead's position when it detonates. Their damage radius and size makes them a good choice for torpedoes and long-range guided missiles with advanced guidance systems.

- Cost: $50
- Mass: 80 (800 kg)

### Large warheads

[![Warhead large](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIABAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAEALAAAAAABAAEAQAICTAEAOw%3D%3D)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/stormworks_gamepedia_en/images/8/83/Warhead_large.png/revision/latest?cb=20220129230344)

These damage everything within 3.5 meters (14 blocks) of the warhead's position when it detonates, though there is also shrapnel which damages other nearby structures. Note that these can be dangerous to carry if not well-protected, as they are large targets and even as little as six shots directly from a rifle (or potentially fewer shots from an autocannon with piercing ammo) can set them off.

- Cost: $100
- Mass: 400 (4,000 kg)

### EMP Warheads

[![EMP warhead](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIABAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAEALAAAAAABAAEAQAICTAEAOw%3D%3D)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/stormworks_gamepedia_en/images/a/a6/EMP_warhead.png/revision/latest?cb=20220129230737)

A nearby EMP warhead being set off will cause vehicles to lose power. EMP range is approximately 500 meters. The brief, faint blue flash and "phwew!" sound can be difficult to notice at the limits of its range, but the effect is unmistakable. Circuit breakers will be tripped, and resetting them will not fix the issue. All electronic actuators and control surfaces will stop working, while all gauges and displays will go blank as if they were unconnected. Power will start coming back on after up to 55 seconds (depending on distance) and ramps back up to full power over five seconds.

Given the radius of the effect on EMP warheads, it is advisable to use a microcontroller to serve as a complex warhead trigger. Data from [radar](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Radar "Radar"), an [impact sensor](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Impact_sensor "Impact sensor"), and friendly vehicle positions transmitted via [radio](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/Wiki/Building/Components/Radio "Wiki/Building/Components/Radio") can be combined to ensure it only detonates when it is within range of the target and *not* within range of friendlies.

- Cost: $200
- Mass: 500 (5,000 kg)

Rocket launchers are highly damaging vehicle-mounted weapons suitable for large and/or stationary targets, like large slow-moving ships. Their damage is very slightly lower yet comparable to a small warhead or an HE shell fired from a battle cannon.

- Cost: $100 (rocket launcher), $50/rocket
- Mass: 50 (500 kg)
- Maximum range: Approx. 2.5 km
- Maximum fire rate: 1 rocket per second (per launcher)
- Speed: ~1000 Blocks per second at launch

For reference, this is a 50% larger damage radius than with heavy autocannons firing HE rounds, and a 3.375x greater volume of damage. They also cause zero recoil and don't require any added loaders/ammo reserves making them a decent choice for minimalist and lightweight vehicles.

Note that the cost of the rockets is not included in the apparent $100 cost of the rocket launcher, but $200 will be charged upon spawning the rocket launcher to cover the cost of the four rockets it contains. Unused rockets on a vehicle are refunded when the vehicle is despawned.

Also note that rocket launchers are poorly suited for high speed or evasive targets. They work best on large, slow moving targets.

Also note that rocket launchers **can not** be reloaded.

Rocket launchers can be edited in XML allowing for many modifications. Changing width changes the spread. Changing length increases the projectile speed and damage. Removing width completely creates an invisible weapon.

## Ballistics Calculations

In Stormworks Search and Destroy, some things should be noted when calculating ballistic data

### Gravity

As of [V1.3.6](https://stormworks.fandom.com/wiki/V1.3.6 "V1.3.6") gravity for projectiles is 30 m/s2. This was intended to improve the ability to use artillery and indirect fire on Stormworks map/battle scales. [In contrast, vehicle gravity is exactly 10 m/s2.]

### Drag

Drag is calculated on a per-tick basis, slowing down projectiles proportional to their speed. To calculate drag per tick:

- Find the current velocity of the projectile (initial velocity can be found elsewhere in this wiki. Velocities after projectile initialization can be derived from previous drag calculations).
- Multiply this velocity by 1 minus the drag coefficient. This is now the projectile's new velocity.

Note that this does not apply for warheads; Calculating drag for warheads is based on how the game processes aerodynamics

Breach opening time (ticks): 305
Shell feeding time (ticks): 240
Breach closing time (ticks): 600
Maximum rate of fire: 3.1 shells/minute
Muzzle velocity: 600 m/s
Projectile lifetime (ticks): 2400
Maximum range: Approx. 7.5 km
Drag Coefficient: 0.0005
Ammo effects:
High explosive (yellow tip): Damages blocks up to 3.75 meters (15 block lengths) from the impact point. No penetration.
Fragmentation (orange tip): Damages blocks up 3.75 meters (15 block lengths) from the impact point and spews shrapnel from the point of impact in all directions. Can penetrate an airgapped wall to spew copious amounts of shrapnel on the other side. The shrapnel itself damages up to about 0.75 m (3 block lengths) from each impact point.
Warheads
With the exception of EMP warheads, all warheads are high explosive. They come in small, medium, and large sizes, and can be activated by receiving damage, by impact (if armed and an impact threshold set), or detonated by logic (when armed and no impact threshold set). Warheads are used to make missiles, bombs, heavy rockets, sea mines, depth charges, torpedoes, and self-destruct devices. Vehicles which are overwhelmingly damaged by an explosion get removed without a trace.
Note that blast damage and range is not increased by underwater detonation.
Small warheads
These damage everything within 2.5 meters (10 blocks) of the warhead's position when it detonates, a slightly greater damage radius than rockets. Well-suited for use as small missile warheads or cluster munitions.
Cost: $25
Mass: 15 (150 kg)
Medium warheads
These damage everything within 3.25 meters (13 blocks) of the warhead's position when it detonates. Their damage radius and size makes them a good choice for torpedoes and long-range guided missiles with advanced guidance systems.
Cost: $50
Mass: 80 (800 kg)
Large warheads
These damage everything within 3.5 meters (14 blocks) of the warhead's position when it detonates, though there is also shrapnel which damages other nearby structures. Note that these can be dangerous to carry if not well-protected, as they are large targets and even as little as six shots directly from a rifle (or potentially fewer shots from an autocannon with piercing ammo) can set them off.
Cost: $100
Mass: 400 (4,000 kg)
EMP Warheads
A nearby EMP warhead being set off will cause vehicles to lose power. EMP range is approximately 500 meters. The brief, faint blue flash and "phwew!" sound can be difficult to notice at the limits of its range, but the effect is unmistakable. Circuit breakers will be tripped, and resetting them will not fix the issue. All electronic actuators and control surfaces will stop working, while all gauges and displays will go blank as if they were unconnected. Power will start coming back on after up to 55 seconds (depending on distance) and ramps back up to full power over five seconds.
Given the radius of the effect on EMP warheads, it is advisable to use a microcontroller to serve as a complex warhead trigger. Data from
radar
, an
impact sensor
, and friendly vehicle positions transmitted via
radio
can be combined to ensure it only detonates when it is within range of the target and
not
within range of friendlies.
Cost: $200
Mass: 500 (5,000 kg)
Rocket launchers
Rocket launchers are highly damaging vehicle-mounted weapons suitable for large and/or stationary targets, like large slow-moving ships. Their damage is very slightly lower yet comparable to a small warhead or an HE shell fired from a battle cannon.
Cost: $100 (rocket launcher), $50/rocket
Mass: 50 (500 kg)
Maximum range: Approx. 2.5 km
Maximum fire rate: 1 rocket per second (per launcher)
Speed: ~1000 Blocks per second at launch
Rocket launchers damage everything within 2.25 meters (9 blocks) of the impact point. For reference, this is a 50% larger damage radius than with heavy autocannons firing HE rounds, and a 3.375x greater volume of damage. They also cause zero recoil and don't require any added loaders/ammo reserves making them a decent choice for minimalist and lightweight vehicles.
Note that the cost of the rockets is not included in the apparent $100 cost of the rocket launcher, but $200 will be charged upon spawning the rocket launcher to cover the cost of the four rockets it contains. Unused rockets on a vehicle are refunded when the vehicle is despawned.
Also note that rocket launchers are poorly suited for high speed or evasive targets. They work best on large, slow moving targets.
Also note that rocket launchers
can not
be reloaded.
Rocket launchers can be edited in XML allowing for many modifications. Changing width changes the spread. Changing length increases the projectile speed and damage.  Removing width completely creates an invisible weapon.
Ballistics Calculations
In Stormworks Search and Destroy, some things should be noted when calculating ballistic data
Gravity
As of
V1.3.6
gravity for projectiles is 30 m/s
2
. This was intended to improve the ability to use artillery and indirect fire on Stormworks map/battle scales. [In contrast, vehicle gravity is exactly 10 m/s
2
.]
Drag
Drag is calculated on a per-tick basis, slowing down projectiles proportional to their speed. To calculate drag per tick:
Find the current velocity of the projectile (initial velocity can be found elsewhere in this wiki. Velocities after projectile initialization can be derived from previous drag calculations).
Multiply this velocity by 1 minus the drag coefficient. This is now the projectile's new velocity.
Note that this does not apply for warheads; Calculating drag for warheads is based on how the game processes aerodynamics
